details:
**Stoning of Stephen**
Stephen, one of seven deacons chosen to serve the Jerusalem community, is tried before the Sanhedrin. After declaring that he sees the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God, he is stoned to death, becoming the first Christian martyr (Acts 7). A young man named Saul watches and approves of the execution.

**Conversion of Saul on the road to Damascus**
Saul, a persecutor of Christians, is struck blind by a light from heaven on the road to Damascus and hears Jesus ask, "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" (Acts 9). A disciple named Ananias restores his sight and baptizes him. Saul, also called Paul, becomes the great missionary apostle whose journeys fill the second half of the book.

**Dedication to Theophilus and Lukan authorship**
Like the Gospel of Luke, Acts opens with a dedication to a man named Theophilus, and both books are traditionally attributed to Luke the Evangelist. Acts is the fifth book of the New Testament, following the four Gospels.

**Pentecost and tongues of fire**
In Acts 2, the Holy Spirit descends on the apostles with a sound like a rushing wind and tongues of fire resting on each of them. They begin speaking in other languages and are understood by a crowd from many nations, and Peter preaches a sermon that converts about three thousand people.

**Matthias chosen by lot**
In Acts 1, the apostles cast lots to choose Matthias as the replacement for Judas Iscariot. Acts describes Judas falling headlong and bursting open, so that all his intestines spilled out.

**Paul at the Areopagus and the "unknown god"**
In Athens, Paul preaches on the Areopagus (Mars Hill), telling the Athenians that the god they honor at an altar "to an unknown god" is the true God (Acts 17). Dionysius the Areopagite is among those who believe.

**Philip, Simon Magus, and the Ethiopian eunuch**
Philip the Evangelist, another of the seven deacons, converts the Samaritan sorcerer Simon Magus, who then tries to buy the power of the Holy Spirit from Peter. The attempt gave the word "simony" its name. Philip is then sent to the road to Gaza, where he baptizes an Ethiopian eunuch, the treasurer of Queen Candace.

**Ananias and Sapphira**
A married couple in the early Jerusalem church who sell land but secretly keep part of the money while claiming to give all of it to the apostles. When Peter confronts them about the lie, each falls dead (Acts 5).

**Shipwreck on Malta and journey to Rome**
The book ends with Paul being taken to Rome as a prisoner to appeal to Caesar. His ship wrecks on Malta, where he survives a viper bite and heals the father of Publius, the island's chief official, of fever and dysentery.

**Peter's vision and Cornelius**
Peter, staying at Joppa, sees a vision of a sheet full of unclean animals and hears a voice say, "Rise, Peter; kill and eat" (Acts 10). Meanwhile an angel tells the Roman centurion Cornelius to send for Peter, and Cornelius and his household become the first Gentile converts baptized by Peter.

**Paul and Barnabas called Zeus and Hermes**
After Paul heals a lame man in Lystra, the crowd takes Paul and Barnabas for the gods Hermes and Zeus and tries to sacrifice to them, and the two tear their clothes in protest (Acts 14). They had been set apart for missionary work by the church at Antioch.

**Earthquake at the Philippi prison**
Paul and Silas, jailed in Philippi, are freed when an earthquake opens the prison doors, but they stay so the jailer will not be punished. The grateful jailer and his household convert (Acts 16).

**Ascension of Jesus**
Acts opens with Jesus ascending into heaven forty days after his resurrection, after promising the disciples that they will receive the Holy Spirit.

**Peter's release from prison and Tabitha**
An angel frees Peter from Herod's prison in Acts 12. Earlier, Peter heals the paralyzed Aeneas and raises the disciple Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead at Joppa (Acts 9).

**Eutychus, Gamaliel, and Priscilla and Aquila**
Eutychus is a young man in Troas who falls asleep during Paul's long sermon, falls from a third-story window, and is restored to life by Paul. Gamaliel is a Pharisee who advises the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone, since a movement from God cannot be stopped. Priscilla and Aquila are tentmakers who host and work with Paul.
